scopes.report: The authorization server now fetches client metadata documents through the root connector, and its consent return check refuses control characters. Three serious defects remain. The consent screen stakes an approval under the raw scope text, but the library spends it under a sorted, defaulted scope set, so unsorted or omitted scopes loop forever. All server state is in-memory per node. Every config reload rebuilds the server, wiping tokens, clients and replay ledgers. Metadata fetches are uncached and unbounded, and refresh tokens never expire. Read fully.

scopes.report: The fixed record carries no content and no price, and its chain, window, signature and amendment walks verify. The node's amendment journal and its durable sink are process-global statics, and the sink is a trait-object seam that the composition root installs into the kernel. The record has no node field, so neither its digest, its signature nor the range read says which node sealed it. After a restart the head read answers with a null head on a non-empty chain and every earlier anchor is gone. The anchor read is never served, and several items are never constructed. Read fully.

scopes.report: The kernel breaker still understands protocols. It classifies HTTP status bands and a gRPC status table, parses the Retry-After header, and names a vendor, a plane and a dialect error code. A second failure can overwrite an armed cooldown and cut short an upstream's Retry-After. Two disagreeing normalizers ship side by side, and the probe journal, warn-once sink and exhaustion helper never run. Read fully.
